join_order.build: aka_name(person_id) → aka_has bitset over name.id space
join_order.notes: FIRST pass. Scan aka_name/person_id.bin (~3.6MB). For each pid in [1..name_N], set aka_has[pid]=1. Output: bitset of ~name_N+1 bytes. Cost: O(901k) sequential reads, dominated by reading one ~3.6MB array. This precedes the name filter so the expensive LIKE only runs on names that could join.

join_order.build: name(filtered: aka_has[id] AND gender='f' AND name LIKE %Ang%) → name_bits over name.id space
join_order.notes: CRITICAL ORDERING: for each name row r, evaluate predicates in cheapest-to-most-expensive order: (1) aka_has[r+1] (1-byte bitset read), (2) gender[r]==gender_code (1-byte read), (3) name LIKE %Ang% (varlen memmem — only reached for ~14% of rows that pass aka_has and ~33% that pass gender). Set name_bits[r+1]=1. NO separate aka_bits is built — the single name_bits already encodes (name predicate AND name has aka_name row). Inner loop tests one bitset instead of two.

join_order.build: title(production_year BETWEEN ylo AND yhi) → trows list of surviving row positions
join_order.notes: Unchanged. ~200k surviving titles drive the outer loop.

join_order.probe: movie_companies via primary CSR on movie_id
join_order.notes: For each title.id v, iterate mc rows in [mc_csr[v], mc_csr[v+1]). Per-row tests in order: note non-empty, company_id in us_bits, then LIKE on (USA)/(worldwide). Break on first match (mc_ok flag).

join_order.probe: movie_info via primary CSR on movie_id
join_order.notes: Per-row tests: info_type_id==release_dates_id (cheapest), then info non-empty, then LIKE Japan:%200% / USA:%200%. Break on first match.

join_order.probe: cast_info via primary CSR on movie_id
join_order.notes: Per-row tests in order: role_id==actress_role_id, person_role_id>=1 (char_name existence — ids dense 1..3140339, so range check IS the semi-join), person_id>=1 && person_id<=name_N && name_bits[person_id] (single bitset test, replaces previous double-test of name_bits AND aka_bits), then note length-switch against the 4 voice literals. On success: read n.name (row = pid-1) and update thread-local MIN(n.name); set any_ci flag so MIN(t.title) is updated once outside the inner ci loop.

filters.predicate: aka_has[id] AND gender=='f' AND name LIKE %Ang%
note NOT NULL AND (LIKE %(USA)% OR LIKE %(worldwide)%) AND company_id in us_bits
info_type_id=release_dates AND info NOT NULL AND (LIKE Japan:%200% OR LIKE USA:%200%)
role_id=actress AND person_role_id>=1 AND name_bits[person_id] AND note IN voice_set

scan.access_pattern: sequential for prefilter; random (CSR-driven) for fact joins

data_structures.aka_has: byte-bitset of size name_N+2 — single-pass build from aka_name/person_id.bin (901k rows)
data_structures.name_bits: byte-bitset of size name_N+2 — encodes (gender match AND name LIKE AND has aka_name row); subsumes the former aka_bits
data_structures.us_bits: byte-bitset of size cn_N+2 over company_name.id
data_structures.trows: vector<int32> of surviving title row positions (~200k)
data_structures.voice_note_set: inline length-switch against 4 string literals — no hash needed
data_structures.aggregation: thread-local {min_name, min_title} string_views; reduce at end. Single-row scalar aggregate, no GROUP BY.

parallelism.notes: aka_has build: parallel scan with byte-stores into bitset (benign race — value is always 1). name_filter: parallel scan, byte-store on success. title prefilter: thread-local vectors then merge. main_scan: dynamic schedule(256) over surviving title rows, thread-local mins reduced at end.

indexes.purpose: row<->id with row = id-1; char_name existence collapses to range check on person_role_id

optimization_notes: Category A (plan restructuring / work elimination). Diagnosis: the dominant phase (name_filter, 12ms of 68ms) ran an expensive memmem LIKE on all 4.17M name rows even though only ~14% have a matching aka_name row and could possibly contribute to the final join. The previous order built name_bits first and then derived aka_bits as a subset — doing the costly work on rows that were doomed to fail the aka_name semi-join anyway. New order: (1) scan aka_name/person_id.bin into aka_has bitset (~3.6MB sequential, ~1-2ms), (2) name filter gated as aka_has[id] && gender==code && LIKE — short-circuit ordering puts the cheapest tests first so memmem only runs for the rare survivor. The two bitsets collapse into one (name_bits encodes name predicate AND has-aka), so the inner ci loop does a single bitset probe instead of two. All other physical choices (primary-CSR range scans into the three fact tables, dense-id arithmetic for char_name existence and name-row recovery, thread-local MIN reduction) are preserved from iter_0 — they were not the bottleneck.
